# Purpose

*A single place that explains **how EcoCommons data is modelled and published** — the data model, attributes, formats and representation — and **what good looks like**, as a set of explicit, checkable rules.*

The first part is a **handbook and style guide** for anyone publishing data to the platform or developing the data architecture and integrations. The second part is the **living rule book**: it turns loose expectations — "titles should be consistent", "every dataset needs a category" — into **explicit, checkable rules**, so that a dataset can be audited objectively rather than by opinion.

Each rule ties back to the metadata fields exposed by the data-ingester index (the same fields we pulled in the [production catalogue audit](ecocommons_prod_data_audit.qmd)):

`title` · `uuid` · `data_category` · `data_subcategories` · `time_domain` · `year` · `resolution` · `spatial_domain` · `spatial_data_type` · `collection_names` · `downloadable` · `created`

::: callout-note
This is a **proposed rule set**, grounded in the [production catalogue audit](ecocommons_prod_data_audit.qmd) of all 58,424 records. Obligations, controlled vocabularies, and the **Current status** figures are offered for EcoCommons / Biosecurity Commons review — confirm and ratify them before any rule is enforced.
:::

# Data standards & publishing handbook

::: callout-important
**Draft.** This handbook is an early draft adapted from the platform's internal data handbook. Sections marked *to be documented* are still being written. It is offered for review and will evolve.
:::

This is a handbook and style guide for data import operations in the platform. It covers the key concepts and conventions for importing a **Dataset** and ensuring its correct representation in the data catalogue and its function with platform models. The intended audience is anyone publishing data to the platform, or developing the data architecture or integrations.

**Further reading.** Full technical description — *EcoCommons / BSC Data Architecture*; *Platform API Reference* (internal references).

## Glossary of terms

| Term | Description |
|------|-------------|
| CRS | Coordinate Reference System (e.g. an EPSG code). |
| Dataset | A structured collection of related information treated as a single unit for analysis, reporting, or computing. |

## Document conventions

This document uses the common technical convention of *Must, Should, May* to convey requirements. Terms such as **Dataset** are bold and capitalised when they refer to the platform model, to distinguish them from general use.

## Overview of the data model

### Dataset

A **Dataset** is a structured collection of related information. In the platform, a Dataset consists of one or more layers, each of which references a physical data file (e.g. a GeoTIFF or CSV).

A Dataset:

-   *May* be spatial, spatiotemporal or aspatial.
-   *May* contain a single layer or multiple layers.
-   *May* be created in series to describe different temporal or spatial variants.
-   *Must* be accompanied by the minimum set of attributes required by the data-catalogue interface.

### Collection

A **Collection** is the highest level of data classification. It represents a group of datasets of common origin. The exact rules of a Collection are not strictly formalised in the platform, but typically a Collection represents related datasets from the same source. Publishers often organise data in terms of a collection, and these relationships should be reflected in the catalogue where possible.

A Collection:

-   *Must* contain datasets from the same publisher or source.
-   *Must* avoid duplication, redundancy or ambiguity with other collections.
-   *Should* not be created for each individual dataset.
-   *May* represent an updated series of publications of the same dataset.
-   *May* represent an informal grouping where no formal one exists.

### Data layers

A **Dataset** consists of one or more **Data Layers**, following common geospatial terminology. For climate and environmental data, layers often map to a structured vocabulary of "variables" (e.g. Mean Temperature → `bioclim_01`). Layers can also be unstructured, using the publisher's own labels or labels adapted to improve readability.

Model inputs such as **SDM** and **Climate Change** *predictors* expect Datasets to follow a structured vocabulary, but many other model inputs do not consider variable names when processing data.

A multi-layer / multi-variable Dataset:

-   *Must* contain layers with consistent spatial properties: resolution, CRS and extent.
-   *May* contain different data types, e.g. `continuous`, `categorical`.
-   *May* contain different data encodings, e.g. `Float32`, `UInt8`.
-   *May* encode variable labels using structured vocabularies or unstructured labels.

#### Layers, variables and parameters

The terms ***layer***, ***variable*** and ***parameter*** are often used interchangeably depending on context, but they all typically refer to a **Data Layer** within the platform model.

| Term | Context |
|------|---------|
| layer | A general term for multi-layer geospatial data. |
| variable | A structured set of terms often used in climate and environmental data to describe specific variables within a system, e.g. "temperature". |
| parameter | The terminology used by CoverageJSON when representing a Data Layer. |

::: callout-note
Variable names can be used as a hint to preselect styles in the platform visualiser.
:::

### Temporal datasets

Generally, climate and environmental Datasets represent a single time interval or aggregate period for all layers (e.g. 2020–2025). This is appropriate for the current EcoCommons models, e.g. SDM and Climate Change.

A Dataset can also represent a temporal series of layers (e.g. `Jan`, `Feb`) where this is supported for a modelling use case. This should not be considered a supported pattern for EcoCommons models to date; however, it is used by Biosecurity Commons models that share the same catalogue.

Temporal data is an area of development that requires further planning at the catalogue and model level.

## Attributes

The data catalogue derives its functionality and value from a set of metadata attributes that accompany the data itself. The platform defines a formal set of attributes for a Dataset; these must be set when publishing data. Not all attributes are required, but applicable attributes should be included to improve the quality and integrity of the data catalogue.

### Sourcing attributes

The publication (e.g. `license`) or domain (e.g. `scientific_name`) attributes of a dataset should typically be transcribed from the publisher source. Other attributes, such as spatial properties, ranges and encoding, are determined automatically during the import process and do not need to be explicitly provided.

The table below illustrates where attributes may be sourced:

| Attribute class | Example | Potential source |
|------|------|------|
| Publication | year | The publisher landing page, or metadata included with data. |
| Domain | taxonomy | The publisher landing page, or metadata included with data. |
| DataType | categorical | Metadata included with data (e.g. an auxiliary XML or other manifest). |
| Spatial | CRS | Extracted from spatial data directly, or provided as metadata. |
| Category | Vegetation | Determined, choosing the most appropriate value, when importing. |

### Style guide

The Dataset `title` and `description` attributes are the most visible part of the catalogue, so a consistent style should be applied.

#### Title

#### Description

*To be documented* — baseline style with example and do's / don'ts.

### Categorisation

::: callout-note
Data categorisation as described here should not be confused with **"categorical data"**, which is a particular spatial data type describing discrete classes of data.
:::

The broadest classification for a Dataset is the `data_category` attribute.

| Category | Examples |
|------|------|
| Topography | DEM data |
| Soil | % Sand, % Silt, % Clay |
| Vegetation | NVIS, BIOMES, NDVI, fractional vegetation cover |
| Freshwater | Streams, lakes |
| Marine | Ocean |
| Human activity | Human population, roads, cities, land use |
| Climate | WorldClim, CliMond, average monthly climate data |
| Biodiversity | Species occurrence data |
| Boundary data | LGAs, countries, NRMs, land parcels |

A secondary classification attribute, `data_subcategories`, allows a list of sub-categories to be assigned to a Dataset. To date this list is not formalised and contains a number of variants — it is closer to an arbitrary tagging system than a formal vocabulary. Data subcategories are presented in the data catalogue for each item; however, they are not currently searchable or browsable. This is a development area to be considered for the catalogue.

### All attributes

The authoritative source of attributes is the Platform Data API reference.

#### General

| Field | Type | Description | Required | Default | Maps to |
|------|------|------|------|------|------|
| `title` | string | Dataset short description | Yes | — | `dct:title` |
| `description` | string | Dataset long description | Yes | — | `dct:description` |
| `data_category` | string | Primary data category | Yes | — | *see category table above* |
| `data_subcategories` | array | Optional secondary data-category labels | No | `[]` | *any* |
| `time_domain` | string | Temporal classification | — | `Current` | `Current`, `Future` |
| `year` | integer | Dataset year | No | `null` | |
| `year_range` | array | Alternative year range in the form `[2000, 2010]` | No | `[]` | |
| `mimetype` | string | Data mimetype | No | `""` | |
| `crs` | string | Coordinate Reference System, e.g. `EPSG:4326` (required for tabular data only) | No | `""` | |
| `resolution` | string | Optional resolution label (e.g. `3 arcmin (~5km)`) | No | `""` | |
| `genre` | string | An internal vocabulary representing scientific / domain detail | No | — | |

#### Publisher

| Field | Type | Description | Required | Default | Maps to |
|------|------|------|------|------|------|
| `license` | string | License short description | Yes | — | `dct:license` |
| `rights` | string | Rights-holder description | Yes | — | `dct:rights` |
| `downloadable` | boolean | Can be directly downloaded | — | `true` | |
| `acknowledgement` | string | Optional additional acknowledgement | No | `""` | |
| `doi` | string | Digital Object Identifier | No | `""` | |
| `source_url` | string | Publisher data source URL | No | `""` | |
| `landing_page` | string | Optional publisher landing page | No | `""` | |
| `attributions` | array of objects | Individual attributions | No | `[]` | |

#### Species

| Field | Type | Description | Required | Default |
|------|------|------|------|------|
| `scientific_name` | string | Scientific name for species data | No | `""` |

#### Climate

| Field | Type | Description | Required | Default |
|------|------|------|------|------|
| `emsc` | string | Emissions scenario (e.g. SSP / RCP) | No | `""` |
| `gcm` | string | Global Circulation Model | No | `""` |

::: callout-note
These attributes should be mapped to [standard terms](https://www.dublincore.org/specifications/dublin-core/dcmi-terms/). For more information see [Darwin Core & Dublin Core](#darwin-core-dublin-core-dcmi) below.
:::

### Data layer / variable attributes

The attributes described so far represent a Dataset as a whole; however, individual layers have their own attributes.

-   A Data Layer *should* provide a human-readable label.
-   A Data Layer *should* provide units where appropriate (e.g. `mean_temperature` → `degC`).
-   A categorical Data Layer *must* provide a table of values that maps values to readable classes.

## Data import

### Supported data formats

| Format | Extension | Supported domain types |
|------|------|------|
| GeoTIFF | `.tif` | Grid |
| GeoPackage | `.gpkg` | Polygon, MultiPolygon |
| CSV | `.csv` | Point |

::: callout-note
The platform can import almost any file format (using the opaque `file` import method). However, this is only useful for specific model cases and has very limited value in the catalogue.
:::

#### GeoTIFF

Single or stacked rasters for either continuous or discrete gridded data. A stacked GeoTIFF is automatically unpacked by the platform during import, so it presents as a multi-layer Dataset.

Cloud-Optimised GeoTIFF (COG) is a compatible variant optimised for use in web environments. The platform does not currently take advantage of this format; however, this may change, so COG is a valid choice when importing data. See [GeoTIFF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeoTIFF).

#### GeoPackage

GeoPackage (GPKG) is an open, non-proprietary, platform-independent and standards-based data format for geographic information systems, built as a set of conventions over a SQLite database. The standard describes conventions for storing vector features, tile matrix sets of imagery, raster maps at various scales, schema and metadata.

The platform does not support all variants of GPKG data. The primary implementation is for polygon data (features); this may be multi-polygon and multi-layer. Additional attributes are imported, but they are currently opaque to the platform in terms of visualisation, and models do not formally use or expect any. See [GeoPackage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeoPackage).

::: callout-note
ESRI Shapefile is also supported; however, it is deprecated and should be avoided for curated data.
:::

#### CSV

CSV files can be imported to represent point data. The basic conventions are described in the platform's data-import interfaces, generally requiring a minimum of a `lat` and `lon` column. Additional fields can be included, but their use is model-specific.

::: callout-note
A spatial CSV file has no standard way of encoding its CRS. It must therefore be provided as an attribute (`crs`) during import, or it will be assumed to be *WGS-84*.
:::

### Import methods

*To be documented* — the API data-import methods.

## Data representation

So far this handbook has described how data is published and presented in the platform catalogue. However, Datasets are also consumed by modelling workflows and other contexts, such as visualisation dashboards. This requires a Dataset and its attributes to be represented in a consistent, portable format. The main representation provided by the platform APIs is **CoverageJSON**.

### CoverageJSON

A coverage is simply a structure that associates positions in space and time with data values. CoverageJSON is designed to encode this information in a form easily consumed by web services. See the [CoverageJSON cookbook](https://covjson.org/cookbook/) and the [OGC Coverage Implementation Schema](https://docs.ogc.org/cs/21-069r2/21-069r2.html).

The platform implements a subset of Coverage domain types:

-   Grid
-   Polygon, MultiPolygon
-   Point

Additionally, a coverage:

-   Describes the spatial domain of the data (resolution, extent, CRS).
-   Represents class information for categorical data.
-   Represents Data Layers as coverage "Parameters", including labels and units.
-   Describes the data encoding and basic metadata, e.g. `min`, `max`, `stddev`.
-   Provides pointers (`rangeAlternates`) for accessing raw data, e.g. `.tif`.

### Darwin Core & Dublin Core (DCMI) {#darwin-core-dublin-core-dcmi}

::: callout-note
This is in early development and has only a minimal implementation at present. Darwin Core in particular currently has no implementation, but is included here for reference.
:::

Coverage provides a standard for spatial data, but says nothing about other data attributes, so another way of representing non-spatial information is required.

**Dublin Core (DCMI)** is a general-purpose, lightweight metadata standard designed to describe any type of digital or physical resource. In practical terms the platform uses it for basic identifiers, e.g. `identifier`, `title`, `description`, `license`, `rights`. The standard uses the namespace prefix `dct:`. This is a machine-readable pattern and allows CoverageJSON and DCMI to coexist in the same document without conflict. Dataset attributes described earlier in the handbook are mapped to appropriate DCMI terms.

**Darwin Core** is an extension of Dublin Core providing a standard for biodiversity data. It includes a conceptual model, specifications and schemas for sharing via various data formats, and a glossary of terms (elsewhere these might be called properties, elements, fields, columns, attributes or concepts) by providing identifiers, labels and definitions.

See [Dublin Core terms](https://www.dublincore.org/specifications/dublin-core/dcmi-terms/) and [Darwin Core](https://dwc.tdwg.org/).

# How to read a rule

Every rule follows the same template so it can be applied and, eventually, automated:

| Field | Meaning |
|-------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| **Rule ID** | Stable identifier (e.g. `MD-001`). |
| **Statement** | The rule itself, phrased as a requirement ("must", "should"). |
| **DCAT-AP** | Obligation + cardinality + the DCAT / DCAT-AP property it maps onto (see [Alignment with DCAT-AP](#alignment-with-dcat-ap)). |
| **Applies to** | Which datasets / fields the rule governs. |
| **Rationale** | Why the rule exists (FAIR, discoverability, interoperability…). |
| **Check** | How to test compliance — a concrete condition. |
| **✅ Pass / ❌ Fail** | An example that satisfies the rule and one that violates it. |

We adopt the **DCAT-AP obligation model**, so severity maps directly onto an accepted standard: **MUST ↔ Mandatory (M)**, **SHOULD ↔ Recommended (R)**, **MAY ↔ Optional (O)**. A property is *Mandatory* exactly when its minimum cardinality is ≥ 1 (cardinality is written `min..max`, e.g. `1..1`, `1..*`, `0..1`).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Alignment with DCAT-AP

[DCAT-AP 3.0](https://semiceu.github.io/DCAT-AP/releases/3.0.0/) describes each dataset property with an **obligation** (Mandatory / Recommended / Optional) and a **cardinality** (`min..max`). We map the EcoCommons index fields onto DCAT / DCAT-AP properties so these rules inherit an accepted standard rather than inventing one. Geospatial specifics (resolution) follow **GeoDCAT-AP**; two fields have no DCAT equivalent and are flagged as **EcoCommons extensions**.

| EcoCommons field | DCAT / DCAT-AP property | DCAT-AP obligation | Card. | Notes |
|------------|------------|------------|------|------------|
| `title` | `dct:title` | Mandatory | 1..\* | — |
| `description` | `dct:description` | Mandatory | 1..\* | Enforced by [`MD-004`](#md-004) |
| `data_category` | `dcat:theme` | Recommended | 0..\* | Bind to an EcoCommons theme vocabulary (local codelist) |
| `data_subcategories` | `dcat:keyword` | Optional | 0..\* | — |
| `time_domain` | `dct:temporal` | Optional | 0..\* | Current / Future / Historical is an EcoCommons **extension** of temporal coverage |
| `year` | `dct:temporal` | Optional | 0..1 | — |
| `spatial_domain` | `dct:spatial` | Optional | 0..\* | Bind to a places codelist (e.g. Countries NAL) |
| `resolution` | `geodcat:spatialResolution` | Optional | 0..1 | **GeoDCAT-AP** |
| `spatial_data_type` | *(none)* | — | — | **EcoCommons extension** (Continuous / Categorical) |
| `collection_names` | `dcat:DatasetSeries` / catalogue membership | — | 0..\* | — |
| `uuid` | `dct:identifier` | Optional | 0..\* | — |
| `created` | `dct:issued` (+ `dct:modified`) | Optional | 0..1 | — |
| `downloadable` | `dcat:Distribution` / `dct:accessRights` | Optional | 0..1 | Access handled at distribution level |

::: callout-tip
Where a rule is **stricter** than DCAT-AP — e.g. we make *category* **MUST**/mandatory though DCAT-AP only *recommends* `dcat:theme` — that is an intentional EcoCommons tightening, and it is noted on the rule.
:::

# 1. Metadata rules

### `MD-001` — Every dataset MUST have a category {#md-001}

> **Statement.** Every dataset **must** populate `data_category` with a value from the controlled vocabulary.
>
> **DCAT-AP.** Obligation **MUST** *(stricter than DCAT-AP, which only recommends `dcat:theme`)* · cardinality `1..*` · aligns to `dcat:theme`.
>
> **Applies to.** All datasets.
>
> **Rationale.** Category drives filtering and discovery in the data explorer; an uncategorised dataset is effectively invisible to users browsing by theme.
>
> **Controlled vocabulary.** `Climate`, `Vegetation`, `Biodiversity`, `Marine`, `Topography`, `Human Activity`, `Freshwater`, `Soil`, `Boundary Data` — the nine categories observed across the production catalogue.
>
> **Check.** A dataset fails if its category is missing, empty, "Unknown", or outside the vocabulary.
>
> **Current status.** **45 of 58,424** records (≈0.08%) are uncategorised/unknown and fail this rule; the remaining 58,379 carry one of the nine values.
>
> ✅ **Pass** — `data_category: "Climate"`\
> ❌ **Fail** — `data_category: ""` or `data_category: "Unknown"`

### `MD-002` — Time domain MUST be a controlled value {#md-002}

> **Statement.** `time_domain` **must** be exactly one of `Current`, `Future`, or `Historical`.
>
> **DCAT-AP.** Obligation **MUST** · cardinality `1..1` · aligns to `dct:temporal` *(EcoCommons classification extension)*.
>
> **Rationale.** Temporal scope is a primary filter for model inputs; free-text or missing values break the "current vs future climate" split.
>
> **Check.** `time_domain ∉ {Current, Future, Historical}` → fail.
>
> **Current status.** All 58,424 records carry a value — `Future` (54,614) or `Current` (3,810); none are missing. `Historical` is defined in the vocabulary but is **currently unused** in production.
>
> ✅ **Pass** — `time_domain: "Future"`\
> ❌ **Fail** — `time_domain: "2050"` or empty.

### `MD-003` — Future datasets SHOULD declare scenario and model {#md-003}

> **Statement.** When `time_domain = "Future"`, the dataset **should** record its emissions scenario and climate model (e.g. `emsc`/`gcm`, or embedded in the title).
>
> **DCAT-AP.** Obligation **SHOULD** · cardinality `0..1` · relates to `dct:temporal` and `dct:title`.
>
> **Rationale.** A future-climate layer is not interpretable without knowing the GCM and SSP/RCP it came from.
>
> ✅ **Pass** — title `"… (2021-2040), HADGEM3-GC31-LL ssp245, 10 arcmin (~20km)"`\
> ❌ **Fail** — title `"Future minimum temperature August"` (no model, no scenario).

### `MD-004` — Every dataset MUST have a description {#md-004}

> **Statement.** Every dataset **must** populate `description` with a non-empty, human-readable summary of what the layer is.
>
> **DCAT-AP.** Obligation **MUST** · cardinality `1..*` · aligns to `dct:description` *(Mandatory in DCAT-AP)*.
>
> **Applies to.** All datasets.
>
> **Rationale.** A title alone rarely conveys provenance, units, or intended use; the description is the primary free-text field search and users rely on. FAIR *Findable* / *Reusable*.
>
> **Check.** A dataset fails if `description` is missing, empty, or merely repeats the title verbatim.
>
> ✅ **Pass** — `description: "WorldClim v2.1 downscaled future minimum temperature for August, 2021-2040, GCM HADGEM3-GC31-LL under SSP2-4.5…"`\
> ❌ **Fail** — `description: ""`

### `MD-005` — Every dataset MUST have a unique identifier {#md-005}

> **Statement.** Every dataset **must** carry a `uuid` that is present and **unique** across the catalogue.
>
> **DCAT-AP.** Obligation **MUST** *(stricter than DCAT-AP, which makes `dct:identifier` Optional)* · cardinality `1..1` · aligns to `dct:identifier`.
>
> **Applies to.** All datasets.
>
> **Rationale.** The `uuid` is the stable key for every per-record API call (`GET /api/dataset/{uuid}`) and is the only field reliable enough to sort/paginate the index on — `_id` and `uuid.keyword` are not. A missing or duplicate `uuid` makes a dataset unaddressable and breaks enumeration.
>
> **Check.** `uuid` empty, or any `uuid` value appearing on more than one record → fail.
>
> **Current status.** All 58,424 records sorted and paged cleanly on `uuid` during the audit — no gaps or collisions observed.
>
> ✅ **Pass** — `uuid: "a3f1c2e4-…"` (unique)\
> ❌ **Fail** — `uuid: ""`, or two records sharing one `uuid`.

### `MD-006` — Datasets SHOULD record an issued date {#md-006}

> **Statement.** Each dataset **should** record when it was added to the catalogue via `created`.
>
> **DCAT-AP.** Obligation **SHOULD** · cardinality `0..1` · aligns to `dct:issued` *(and `dct:modified` on change)*.
>
> **Applies to.** All datasets.
>
> **Rationale.** An issued date lets users and auditors reason about freshness and change over time, and underpins "what's new since…" views.
>
> **Check.** `created` missing or unparseable as a date → fail (SHOULD, so advisory).
>
> ✅ **Pass** — `created: "2024-11-03T09:12:00Z"`\
> ❌ **Fail** — `created: ""`

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 2. Naming & title standards

### `NM-001` — Titles SHOULD follow the canonical pattern {#nm-001}

> **Statement.** Dataset titles **should** follow the canonical pattern: *Source/Product, variable (period), model/scenario, resolution*.
>
> **DCAT-AP.** Obligation **SHOULD** · aligns to `dct:title` *(which DCAT-AP makes Mandatory, `1..*` — presence is assumed; this rule governs its **form**)*.
>
> **Rationale.** A predictable title structure makes long lists scannable and sortable, and lets users compare like-for-like layers across products.
>
> ✅ **Pass** — `"WorldClim v2.1, future climate Minimum Temperature August (2021-2040), HADGEM3-GC31-LL ssp245, 10 arcmin (~20km)"`\
> ❌ **Fail** — `"min temp aug worldclim"`

### `NM-002` — Resolution MUST use the standard notation {#nm-002}

> **Statement.** `resolution` **must** be expressed as `<value> <unit> (~<approx>)`, e.g. `10 arcmin (~20km)`, `30 arcsec (~1km)`.
>
> **DCAT-AP.** Obligation **MUST** · cardinality `0..1` · aligns to `geodcat:spatialResolution` *(GeoDCAT-AP)*.
>
> **Rationale.** Consistent resolution strings let users match datasets to a target grid and are machine-parseable.
>
> ✅ **Pass** — `"30 arcsec (~1km)"`\
> ❌ **Fail** — `"1km"`, `"0.0083 deg"`, empty.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 3. Data standards

### `DS-001` — Spatial data type MUST be declared {#ds-001}

> **Statement.** `spatial_data_type` **must** be one of `Continuous` or `Categorical`.
>
> **DCAT-AP.** Obligation **MUST** · cardinality `1..1` · **EcoCommons extension** (no DCAT-AP equivalent).
>
> **Rationale.** Downstream models treat continuous and categorical predictors differently; misclassification silently corrupts results.
>
> ✅ **Pass** — `spatial_data_type: "Continuous"`\
> ❌ **Fail** — missing, or a numeric/other value.

### `DS-002` — Every dataset MUST belong to a collection {#ds-002}

> **Statement.** `collection_names` **must** be non-empty.
>
> **DCAT-AP.** Obligation **MUST** · cardinality `0..*` · aligns to `dcat:DatasetSeries` / catalogue membership.
>
> **Rationale.** Collections are how related layers are grouped for users; orphan datasets (`None`) are hard to find and to govern.
>
> **Check.** `collection_names` empty or `["None"]` → fail.
>
> **Current status.** Production holds ~54 collections; the catalogue is heavily skewed — **WorldClim-v2.1 alone accounts for 52,308 records (≈90%)**, so most datasets are well-placed, but orphan checks matter for the long tail.
>
> ✅ **Pass** — `collection_names: ["WorldClim-v2.1"]`\
> ❌ **Fail** — `collection_names: []`

### `DS-003` — Spatial domain SHOULD be declared {#ds-003}

> **Statement.** `spatial_domain` **should** be populated from a places codelist (e.g. `Australia`, `Global`, a state/territory).
>
> **DCAT-AP.** Obligation **SHOULD** · cardinality `0..*` · aligns to `dct:spatial`.
>
> **Applies to.** All datasets.
>
> **Rationale.** Geographic extent is a primary discovery filter; a layer with no declared spatial domain cannot be found by "data for Australia" queries and risks being applied outside its valid footprint.
>
> **Check.** `spatial_domain` empty, or a value outside the agreed places codelist → fail (advisory).
>
> ✅ **Pass** — `spatial_domain: "Australia"`\
> ❌ **Fail** — `spatial_domain: ""`

### `DS-004` — Access MUST be declared explicitly {#ds-004}

> **Statement.** `downloadable` **must** be an explicit boolean (`true` / `false`), never absent or blank.
>
> **DCAT-AP.** Obligation **MUST** · cardinality `1..1` · aligns to `dcat:Distribution` / `dct:accessRights` *(declared at the dataset level here)*.
>
> **Applies to.** All datasets.
>
> **Rationale.** Users and tooling need to know up front whether a layer can be exported; an undefined access flag forces a trial-and-error download attempt and breaks automated harvesting.
>
> **Check.** `downloadable` missing or non-boolean → fail.
>
> ✅ **Pass** — `downloadable: true`\
> ❌ **Fail** — `downloadable: null` or absent.

# References & prior art

This rule book is deliberately lightweight, but it follows the same pattern as established metadata and data-quality standards: each field carries an **obligation level** (mandatory / recommended / optional) and is often bound to a **controlled vocabulary (codelist)**. The standards below are the best templates to align with — and, over time, to borrow controlled vocabularies from.

### Geospatial metadata & quality standards

-   **ISO 19115-1** (geographic metadata) and **ISO 19157** (data quality) — the mainstream geospatial standard. Elements carry Mandatory / Conditional / Optional obligations (the analogue of our MUST / SHOULD / MAY) and bind to codelists. *Normative text is paywalled by ISO;* open overviews: [DCC guide](https://www.dcc.ac.uk/resources/metadata-standards/iso-19115) · [ICA wiki](https://wiki.icaci.org/index.php?title=ISO_19115-1:2014_Geographic_information_-_Metadata_-_Part_1:_Fundamentals).
-   **FGDC CSDGM** — the long-standing US Content Standard for Digital Geospatial Metadata, same obligation model: [fgdc.gov/metadata/csdgm-standard](https://www.fgdc.gov/metadata/csdgm-standard).
-   **INSPIRE metadata (EU)** — ships an official online **validator** that reports pass/fail against the rules; the automatable end-state of our *Check* field: [inspire.ec.europa.eu/validator](https://inspire.ec.europa.eu/validator/).

### Catalogue / FAIR profiles (closest to this Rule Book's format)

-   **DCAT-AP** — a W3C DCAT application profile defining per-field **cardinalities and obligations** plus recommended controlled vocabularies. The closest structural match to this page (see [Alignment with DCAT-AP](#alignment-with-dcat-ap) above): [DCAT-AP 3.0 spec](https://semiceu.github.io/DCAT-AP/releases/3.0.0/) · [W3C DCAT](https://www.w3.org/TR/vocab-dcat-3/).
-   **GeoDCAT-AP** — the geospatial extension of DCAT-AP (adds spatial resolution, reference system, etc.), the source for our `resolution` mapping: [GeoDCAT-AP](https://semiceu.github.io/GeoDCAT-AP/releases/).
-   **FAIR principles** — the guiding rationale (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable): [go-fair.org/fair-principles](https://www.go-fair.org/fair-principles/).

### Ecology / biodiversity domain standards (relevant to EcoCommons)

-   **Darwin Core** — biodiversity occurrence data terms: [dwc.tdwg.org](https://dwc.tdwg.org/).
-   **EML — Ecological Metadata Language** — dataset metadata for ecology: [eml.ecoinformatics.org](https://eml.ecoinformatics.org/).

### Making rules machine-checkable

-   **SHACL** — validate RDF / DCAT metadata against constraint "shapes": [w3.org/TR/shacl](https://www.w3.org/TR/shacl/).
-   **Frictionless Data (Table Schema)** — declarative field/row validation for tabular data: [frictionlessdata.io](https://frictionlessdata.io/).
